messages.author: a348b46e3f098487
messages.subject: Help with BioGeoBEARS Package Installation
parts:
Dear colleagues,

I am having some challenges installing BioGeoBEARS. I first followed the tutorial available at phylo.wikidot (http://phylo.wikidot.com/biogeobears#installation), but had problems with packages (including BioGeoBEARS) not compatible with the installed R version (3.6.1). So I tried the tutorial available on GitHub (https://github.com/nmatzke/BioGeoBEARS) but it's not working either. I was also guided by the latest instructions from this forum, but I had no success.
Following the GitHub tutorial I was able to install the "rexpokit" and "cladoRcpp" packages without any problem. The challenge starts when I try to install the devtools package. The "devtools" package has been partially installed resulting in 40 warnings, without being possible to use. After this step when tried to install the "BiogeoBEARS" package I always get the message that the package is not available for my R version. However, I tried for many R versions (from 3.0 to 3.6). So I kindly come to you for any help that might lead me to success to use BioGeoBEARS!

Thank you very much,

Fábio Oliveira

messages.author: 115d05260b0c341a
messages.subject: Re: [BioGeoBEARS] Help with BioGeoBEARS Package Installation
parts:
Hi -- it sounds like the problem is with devtools -- this is quite surprising as it is a widely-used package done by professional programmers.  I would post your devtools warnings/errors to here:
https://github.com/r-lib/devtools/issues

Re: BioGeoBEARS, another method is to install from source:

1. Go to: https://github.com/nmatzke/BioGeoBEARS

2. Click "Clone or Download"

3. Download the .zip file

4. unzip it

5. install.packages(pkgs="/Users/nmat471/Downloads/BioGeoBEARS-master", repos=NULL, type="source")

(replace "/Users/nmat471/Downloads/BioGeoBEARS-master" with your unzipped folder)

Cheers,
Nick
